  "api_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/element-hq/riot-android/issues/2346",
  "title": "Privacy - Avatar and shown name - no options",
  "body": "Hi, as it seems like there is only support for one user picture (which can everybody see) - I thought to ask if that is gonna change at some point.\n\nA user might want to use a personal picture that personal friends/family can only see, while public/all others see another - without face e.g..\n\nIs there any support in Matrix for this or if not, is there any way this privacy option may get added? This is currently a public leaking bit of information.",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2018-06-07T05:36:34Z",
  "updated_at": "2019-08-21T12:06:33Z",
  "state": "open",
  "closed_at": null,
  "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T06:24:05.564181+00:00",
  "comments_fetched_at": [
    "2026-11-05T06:24:05.564181+00:00"
  ],
  "expected_comment_count": 5,
  "retrieved_comment_count": 5,
  "comments_complete": true,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 395407930,
      "url": "https://github.com/element-hq/riot-android/issues/2346#issuecomment-395407930",
      "created_at": "2018-06-07T12:48:11Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-06-07T12:50:55Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "Matrix supports it, Riot does not.\n\nI recommend opening an issue on Riot-Web as well, as that leads the design and the features. The mobile clients follow behind.\n\nBy the way, you can manually change your avatar in a single room using Riot-Web's /devtools. Maybe ask FAQBot about it."
    },
    {
      "id": 395458183,
      "url": "https://github.com/element-hq/riot-android/issues/2346#issuecomment-395458183",
      "created_at": "2018-06-07T15:15:12Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-06-07T15:15:59Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "I dont want to change room picture to be my picture. than when I open chat all I see is myself avatar, and not the one of the chat partner I do chat with (in 1:1 direct chats). Are we talking about the same thing?"
    },
    {
      "id": 402066911,
      "url": "https://github.com/element-hq/riot-android/issues/2346#issuecomment-402066911",
      "created_at": "2018-07-03T09:05:54Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I don't think you understand. Have a look at this: https://vault.webdevguru.co.uk/Matrix/per-room-nickname/"
    },
    {
      "id": 402085396,
      "url": "https://github.com/element-hq/riot-android/issues/2346#issuecomment-402085396",
      "created_at": "2018-07-03T09:53:40Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-03T10:14:12Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "No, this is initially mainly about picture not realname. Too the main expectation is not room based, but global. I'm extending the title to reflect that.\n\nReal example from myself:\nHave a matrix account with public known username, and association with my realname.\nNow I want to chat with my father and others from family over Matrix. Non-Techies - this means they expect to see just my name and a real face icon.\n\nFor this father has a public unknown username, nothing that would identify a relation with myself, or give details about him.\n\nIn any situation its the goal that I can see his face picture (where no avatar at all should be public) and his real displayname. The same goes the other way round, and with other family members.\n\nThis is currently not possible, and thats why I reported this. What I call Privacy in most important level - to use Matrix without leaving public identifiable information.\n\nOther protocols/messengers usually have an Option to set visibility for:\n* Nobody/ Everybody\n* Specific persons (users)\n* Groups (Rooms)\n\n\nAnd thats what I expect from Matrix protocol and clients to support too. Maybe not all cases, but the example with father has the main goals. This is nothing I see as optional feature, but a basic need.\nI don't know what is currently possible or planned but I do hope, Matrix as speaking for open, decentralization and privacy does get an solution for this."
    },
    {
      "id": 523427260,
      "url": "https://github.com/element-hq/riot-android/issues/2346#issuecomment-523427260",
      "created_at": "2019-08-21T12:06:33Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "The per-room avatar and nickname are definitely critical features. Adding an option to edit your nickname per-room without the devtools would be an excellent and relatively simple start for this, then get started on the avatar options."
    }
  ],

    "body": "I second this request for choosing a displayname per room.\n\nIn https://matrix.org/jira/browse/SPEC-230 it’s given ‘not high priority’. One of the key features of Matrix however is to bridge networks and combine things. Many people use different (nick)names and aliases on different networks, fora and so on. People often (obligatory) use surnames for work, but first names to communicate with family and friends.\n\nSo shouldn’t this request get a (much) higher priority?\n",
    "created_at": "2016-10-17T10:00:42Z",
    "updated_at": "2022-10-10T15:32:34Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034670,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034670",
    "body": "the priority here is basically \"not high relative to stuff like e2e\". it's prolly somewhere between p2 and p3; will put it as p2 for now.\n",
    "created_at": "2016-11-06T01:48:30Z",
    "updated_at": "2016-11-06T01:48:30Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034672,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034672",
    "body": "Per-group nicks, rather than per-channel, would make more sense, when groups are done.     "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034805",
    "body": "In a self-hosted home server local rooms may be OK with a recognisable name as the users may know each other within their organisation, but rooms federated into that homeserver perhaps not so.\r\nCould there be a setting as simple as \"Homeserver Name\" \"Federated Alias\"?\r\n",

    "id": 1172034808,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034808",
    "body": "Why don't just add the scope, i.e current room, to the existing /nick command in Riot?\r\nOr even better add this functionality to /nick clone /localnick or /roomnick or /displayname.\r\n\r\nTo be specific roomId could be passed to [setDisplayName](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-react-sdk/blob/37c984e1955185fc1d915b8620ec506dad177959/src/SlashCommands.js#L95), and [setDisplayName](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-js-sdk/blob/76c675cd09685664bc63883a881eed8808b3911f/src/client.js#L1865) could pass name to the [_membershipChange](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-js-sdk/blob/76c675cd09685664bc63883a881eed8808b3911f/src/client.js#L1809) based on roomID status.\r\nAny takers @ara4n?",

  },

    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034816",
    "body": "Now that we have this for rooms, it would be great to also have this for communities. Such that if someone starts a new chat with me, they will see my community name in those new rooms as well, and not my general one.",

Such that if someone starts a new chat with me, they will see my community name in those new rooms as well, and not my general one.\r\n\r\nThe issue there is a room can be in 0-N communities, so what if Room X is in 100 communities, which Display Name do we use?",

    "body": "> \r\n> \r\n> @fladd\r\n> \r\n> > Now that we have this for rooms, it would be great to also have this for communities. Such that if someone starts a new chat with me, they will see my community name in those new rooms as well, and not my general one.\r\n> \r\n> The issue there is a room can be in 0-N communities, so what if Room X is in 100 communities, which Display Name do we use?\r\n\r\nThe nickname that was last set and affected that room.",

    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034826",
    "body": "To elaborate on this:\r\n\r\nSuppose you have Rooms X and Y, and communities 1 and 2:\r\n1(X,Y)\r\n2(Y)\r\n\r\nIf I now change nickname in community 1, then it is also changed in X and Y.\r\nIf I then change it directly in X, then is is changed only there.\r\nIf I then change nickname in community 2, then room Y is changed.\r\n\r\nChanging community nickname should also affect the community user list, and any new (1to1) room that is created from within a community. That is, the nickname should be inherited.",

    "body": "> and any new (1to1) room that is created from within a community.\r\n\r\nwill probably be the trickiest, as starting a 1:1 with someone in a community is no different than starting one with someone manually, so there's no way for anything to know that it should pick up that name",

    "id": 1172034935,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034935",
    "body": "There is a list with user names on the community page. If you start a chat from that list I meant. Otherwise, the 1to1 chat should of course just inherit the nickname from the room you started the chat from (if started from a room; otherwise default nickname).",
    "created_at": "2019-02-26T11:59:13Z",

    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034937",

Otherwise, the 1to1 chat should of course just inherit the nickname from the room you started the chat from (if started from a room; otherwise default nickname).\r\n\r\n\r\nI know what you mean, but when you start a chat with that list there's no special API for starting a chat in a community/room, its just create a room and invite the other user, the other user then chooses their display name and have no idea what screen you were looking at in your client when you were starting the chat.",
    "created_at": "2019-02-26T12:01:17Z",
    "updated_at": "2019-02-26T12:01:17Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034938,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034938",
    "body": "mmh, I see. That unfortunately makes the feature of setting room-based nicknames not very useful.",
    "created_at": "2019-02-26T12:03:45Z",
    "updated_at": "2019-02-26T12:03:45Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034940,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034940",
    "body": "Matrix communities just being a collection of random rooms, is totally different from discord communities, where the rooms are owned, and specific to that community. \r\n\r\nSo with discord you can do things like have a name per community, limit access and abilities by roles, etc. Whereas in matrix you have to do this for every room... which is more work, but it makes sense when you consider that one room can be a part of many communities. \r\n\r\nI will say tho that it is easier to \"onboard\" ppl the discord way, but its def less flexible and normalized. A good compromise might be a way to mass invite ppl to all the rooms in a community, if they're private for example, and a `/communitynick` command that could search for your user thats in all the rooms of that community, and rename you in them.\r\n",
    "created_at": "2019-02-26T17:18:47Z",
    "updated_at": "2019-02-26T17:18:47Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034941,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034941",
    "body": "@t3chguy \r\n\r\n> If you're using riot Web it's possible to do roughly scripts. See https://vault.webdevguru.co.uk/Matrix/per-room-nickname/\r\n\r\nThis works. Thanks. Is there anything similar for display pictures? :)\r\n\r\n",

    "updated_at": "2019-05-09T16:33:15Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034947,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034947",
    "body": "> @t3chguy\r\n> \r\n> > If you're using riot Web it's possible to do roughly scripts. See https://vault.webdevguru.co.uk/Matrix/per-room-nickname/\r\n> \r\n> This works. Thanks. Is there anything similar for display pictures? :)\r\n\r\nThe same thing except you update the `avatar_url` instead",

    "updated_at": "2019-05-09T16:45:44Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034951,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034951",
    "body": "> The same thing except you update the `avatar_url` instead\r\n\r\nIt isn't working. I tried using this image.\r\n\r\nhttps://images.pexels.com/photos/158056/water-mountain-moon-river-158056.jpeg\r\n\r\nIt just says: \"alittlebitofit changed their profile picture\" but doesn't actually show the picture.\r\n\r\n",
    "created_at": "2019-05-09T17:27:31Z",
    "updated_at": "2019-05-09T17:27:31Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034953,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034953",
    "body": "You need to use an `mxc://` URL. You can get one by uploading that image in some room then clicking \"View Source\" on the image message. Then under `content->file->url` there should be an `mxc://...` URL. Copy and use that as the value for `avatar_url`.",
    "created_at": "2019-05-09T17:52:36Z",
    "updated_at": "2019-05-09T17:52:36Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034958,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034958",
    "body": "> You need to use an `mxc://` URL. You can get one by uploading that image in some room then clicking \"View Source\" on the image message. Then under `content->file->url` there should be an `mxc://...` URL. Copy and use that as the value for `avatar_url`.\r\n\r\nUnder \"View Source\", you need to check for `content->url`, there's no `file` thing in between.\r\nAlthough its working, but why do I need the `mxc://` URL?\r\nAnd btw what does 'mxc' stand for?",
    "created_at": "2019-05-11T06:02:52Z",
    "updated_at": "2019-05-11T06:02:52Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034959,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034959",
    "body": "`content->file->url` is under \"View Decrypted Source\", meaning that the image is in an encrypted room. And that particular image has no `url` under \"View Source\".\r\n\r\nAlso I found multiple `url`s under \"View Decrypted Source\", I tried them all, and riot simply says `alittlebitofit changed their profile picture` but I see nothing changed.\r\n\r\nSo the only solution that seemed to work was to upload the image in an \"unencrypted\" room which I did not want to, yet I tried. And it worked. But later when I deleted that image from the (unencrypted) room, my profile picture disappeared.\r\n\r\nSo here I am again, back to square 1 😅.",
    "created_at": "2019-05-11T06:54:47Z",
    "updated_at": "2022-10-10T15:32:36Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 1172034964,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172034964",
    "body": "@alittlebitofit mxc stands for matrix content, it is a file that is uploaded to a matrix server and available for other servers in the federation to access.     "body": "Nah, since as @t3chguy said, it's not associated with the keys to decrypt that content.\n\nSo while you can see it as part of a message, when Riot loads in the image for your avatar it doesn't expect an encrypted image, and thus doesn't try to decrypt it.     "id": 1172035217,
    "html_url": "https://github.com/element-hq/element-meta/issues/499#issuecomment-1172035217",
    "body": "I want to add my suggestions of some design and implementation thoughts to this thread now that t3chguy pointed me here.\r\n\r\nMy suggestion goes into more detail that includes proposals for changes in spec and server and can be found at vector-im/element-meta#370, but let me summarize the element part here:\r\n\r\n- proper per-room display names are required for reasons including but not limited to privacy and some glamour (this is supposed to be fun, dammit!)\r\n- display names should be properly manageable including a default, per room (GUI), and upcoming spaces. current state of this is not only missing GUI, but also bad UX that changing your global display name or avatar requires your homeserver to reset it in all rooms you're a member of per the spec\r\n- the core of my proposal: allow to choose the room display name upon joining. suggestions may be offered based on existing display names. this seems to require spec and server changes.\r\n- considerations for fallbacks are necessary\r\n\r\nAgain, find more details and reasoning at vector-im/element-meta#370.",
